subject: Location assurance, pinning options, and failover/backups — Marin Health follow-up
messages:
From: Lena Rivera <lena.rivera@marinhealth.org>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Cho <mike.cho@marinhealth.org>
Date: Sat, 24 Oct 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up — data location & failover items from today

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. A couple of follow-ups from our security and procurement teams so we can move to a mutual action plan:

1) Location/pinning: Our PHI flows must remain within US boundaries unless a contractual exception is granted. Can you confirm whether Redwood can enforce a strict US-only pin (no cross-region replication of data) and still provide an RTO/RPO acceptable for our clinical use?

2) Cross-region failover: We understand warm-standby options exist — we need the exact behaviors: in a failover event, will live request routing move to an APAC/EU replica that contains decrypted KV cache or only read-only snapshots? Any cross-border transfer must be consented and logged.

3) Backups & retention: We need default retention windows for system logs, request traces, and generated artifact retention. Our security team would like a 90-day retention for request logs and a clearly defined purging process for request content containing PII.

4) Key management / encryption: Do you offer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) that ensure keys never leave our control? For auditors we need confirmation that Redwood employees do not have access to plaintext model inputs/outputs if CMK is enabled.

5) Evidence for compliance: Can you share the SOC2 summary and a concise statement we can include in our procurement packet describing where data is stored and how failover behaves?

Next steps: if you can send a short one-pager addressing 1–4 and proposed next steps with owners and dates, we can circulate internally and book a follow-up.

— Lena
Lena Rivera
Director, IT Security | Marin Health

Attachments: MarinSecurityQuestionnaire.xlsx (referenced)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Follow-up — data location & failover items from today

Lena — thanks for the clear list and for taking time today. High-level answers below; I attached a short datasheet and the SOC2 summary for your procurement/audit team. I’ll loop Aditya (SE) on technical details and Ben on contracting cadence.

1) Strict US pinning: Yes — Redwood supports strict region pinning. For Marin Health we can configure a US-only deployment where production compute, storage, and snapshots are provisioned in US regions only. No cross-region replication occurs unless explicitly enabled via an agreed contract clause.

2) Cross-region failover behavior: We offer two patterns you can choose from:
   - Manual failover (recommended for strict data boundary customers): standby capacity exists in a secondary region but is kept offline; failover requires operator approval (audit trail + time to failover). No live cross-region transfer of decrypted KV or session state prior to authorization.
   - Controlled automated failover (for customers who accept limited cross-region action): warm-standby can be kept synced with encrypted snapshots; on failover the replica will be brought online and failover events are logged and require a configured policy (notify/auto-accept).

3) Backups & retention:
   - Default request trace retention: 90 days (configurable to 30/90/365).
   - Generated artifact retention (model outputs stored for debugging): configurable; default 30 days unless you opt-in to longer retention for evaluation.
   - Purging: we support automated purge jobs and on-demand deletion. We’ll provide a purge runbook and an API to trigger retention policy changes.

4) Key management / encryption:
   - Customer-managed keys (KMS) supported via cloud KMS or customer HSM integrations. If CMK is enabled, keys are held in your KMS and Redwood cannot decrypt content without your key (you control rotation and revocation).
   - Access controls: audit logs show any administrative key use. We’ll produce a short statement for your auditors describing the CMK workflow.

5) Evidence: attaching redwood-soc2-summary.pdf. I’ll also prepare a 1-page location assurance summary tailored to Marin Health with explicit statements about pinning and failover behavior.

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Marin to share a short list of PII types and sample non-production data (Lena / Mike) — due by 2026-10-29.
- Redwood to deliver 1-page Location Assurance + purge runbook (Olga / Aditya) — target 2026-10-27.
- Technical deep-dive on failover behavior with SEs (Aditya) — proposed 2026-10-29 or 2026-10-30.

I’ve attached the datasheet and SOC2 summary here. If those timelines work, I’ll set the follow-up.

Best,

Hi Mike / Lena — quick technical clarifications to include in the 1-pager and the runbook Olga mentioned:

- Manual failover RTO/RPO:
  * Manual failover (US-pinned): typical RTO target 1–2 hours for operator-driven promotion of standby; RPO near-zero if we keep active replication within-region. If you require stricter RTO we can design a warm-standby kept in a ready state (shorter RTO, documented cost impact).

- CMK and logs: when CMK is enabled, request payloads are encrypted before they reach persistent logs; access logs and request traces will contain metadata (timestamps, model, token counts, request id) but not plaintext inputs/outputs. Any debug captures that would contain plaintext require an explicit on-the-record export and are gated by your CMK permissions and an approval workflow.

- Snapshot/replication geography: encrypted snapshots can be stored in designated US-only buckets when you select US-only pinning. We will not replicate encrypted snapshots to EU/APAC unless you enable cross-region replication in writing.

- Auditability: we provide an audit trail for any failover action, key use (when using CMK) and retention policy changes. Audit logs include who initiated the action, timestamps, and affected resource IDs.

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Draft RTO/RPO table for manual vs warm-standby (to be included in the 1-pager).
- Short CMK audit statement for your contract team.

I’ll attach those small snippets to the runbook Olga will produce. Happy to do the technical deep-dive next week (30–45 minutes).

Thanks,
